<p>
        These are the questions still genuinely undecided. The list shrank
        between drafts as previously-open issues got resolved into spec
        sections — see "Resolved since draft 2" at the bottom for
        traceability.
      </p>

      <h3>Still open</h3>

      <ol>
        <li>
          <strong>UI plugin install flow when the host isn't running.</strong> If the host UI is offline, the CLI can still drive install (`papercusp install` doesn't require the GUI), but capability prompts are text-only. Is text-only consent acceptable for high-tier capabilities (§10.6.1), or should the spec require GUI confirmation for those? Affects headless deployments.
        </li>
        <li>
          <strong>Versioning of the spec itself.</strong> Plugin manifests pin against a substrate <em>service</em> version (§8.4.1), but not against a <em>spec</em> version. How do we evolve the harness contract (add a 5th required role, change state schema) without breaking installed plugins? Likely needs a `papercusp` field in the manifest pinning a spec semver range, with the same evolution rules as services.
        </li>
        <li>
          <strong>Goal-graph richness.</strong> Today goals are a tree (parent_id). Real strategy involves multiple goals contributing to one outcome (DAG, not tree). Add multiple parents? Weighted contributions? Or punt to plugins?
        </li>
        <li>
          <strong>Reputation and reviews.</strong> §11.6 establishes verified vs unverified trust tiers based on identity + signature, but no mechanism for community feedback. Does the marketplace need ratings, reviews, or a reporting flow for low-quality (not malicious) packages? At what scale does this become necessary, and who moderates?
        </li>
      </ol>

      <h3>Resolved since draft 2</h3>

      <p>
        These were open questions in earlier drafts; the linked sections
        now answer them.
      </p>

      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Was open</th><th>Now answered in</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr>
            <td>Plugin-defined decision verbs — should plugins extend the verb vocabulary beyond a fixed built-in set, and how is it kept bounded/auditable?</td>
            <td>§6 (orchestrator) — verb vocabulary is <strong>per-blueprint</strong>, not fixed: each blueprint declares its own verbs in <code>spine.edges</code> (a <code>verb → action</code> map), parsed by <code>parseDecisionFor</code> and interpreted by the data-lookup engine <code>deriveNext</code> (D-002, "pipeline-as-data"). Boundedness/auditability is enforced by spine validation (<code>validateDeciderSpine</code>: terminal reachability + declared-role checks). The built-in coding pipeline still ships a <em>fixed</em> set, classified by an exhaustive switch. Note the emitter is the per-feature <code>director</code> (in the <code>coding-factory</code> blueprint), not a single "orchestrator"; the Pot (<code>coding</code>) layer has no spine and emits no <code>NEXT_*</code> verbs.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>LLM-agnosticism — the runtime hardcodes Claude; should the spec require pluggable LLM providers (adapter slot)?</td>
            <td>Reference runtime already ships the adapter slot. Three pluggable agent backends (<code>claude-code</code>, <code>omp</code>, <code>codex</code>) each carry their own config-driven invocation command and stream parser; the backend and command are config fields, not hardcoded. <code>claude-code</code> is the <em>default</em>, not the only option.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Multi-tenancy in the runtime — how to scope user/install when many run side-by-side</td>
            <td>§10.5 — shared-DB multi-tenancy: a single <code>harness_shared</code> schema whose tables are tenant-keyed by <code>install_slug</code> / <code>workspace_id</code> and isolated by row-level-security policies (<code>workspace_id = current_setting('app.workspace_id')</code>), not a per-install database.</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Marketplace governance — moderation model for malicious entries; reviewer approval at publish time?</td>
            <td>§11.6 (namespace policy + verified/unverified trust tiers via signing) + §11.9 (retraction levels: deprecated / yanked / withdrawn / quarantined, with operator-only quarantine for security incidents)</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Permission fatigue — how to prevent users from blindly approving 30-cap manifests</td>
            <td>§10.6 (impact-tiered budgets + grouped consent + default-deny new caps at update)</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Cost containment for routines — how to prevent a buggy cron from draining LLM budget</td>
            <td>§9.4 (per-routine rate limit + per-plugin daily budget + system-wide caps + auto-pause on 5 errors)</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Plugin update flow — what happens when a new version requests new capabilities or migrates schema</td>
            <td>§11.7 (CLI flow with capability diff and snapshot) + §10.8 (per-change-class semantics)</td>
          </tr>
          <tr>
            <td>Hook ordering when multiple plugins fight for the same hook</td>
            <td>§8.5.1 (named predicates as canonical, integer priorities as fallback)</td>
          </tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
